# Ignoring Files

## Not everything belongs in Git

Git is built for tracking the files you author. Some files are better left [untracked]{.uwred}:

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

- [Scratch and throwaway files]{.uwred} — temporary notes, drafts, scratch output
- [Large or raw data]{.uwred} — bloats the repo and rarely changes
- [Binary files]{.uwred} — Git can't meaningfully `diff` a photo or `.xlsx`; it just stores a full copy each time
- [Secrets]{.uwred} — API keys, passwords, credentials should never be committed

<div class="gap-md"></div>

Instead of eyeballing `git status` and carefully avoiding them, we can tell Git to ignore them for good.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Bucky's folder gets cluttered

Game-day prep leaves a mess: scratch files and a folder of receipt photos.

```bash
touch scratch.tmp shopping-draft.tmp
mkdir receipts
touch receipts/costco.jpg receipts/metcalfe.jpg
```

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

The `.tmp` files are throwaway scratch; the `receipts/` photos are big, binary, and nobody needs them in the menu's history.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Git sees the clutter

```bash
git status
```

```
On branch main
Untracked files:
  (use "git add <file>..." to include in what will be committed)
	receipts/
	scratch.tmp
	shopping-draft.tmp

nothing added to commit but untracked files present (use "git add" to track)
```

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

Git keeps nagging about files we never intend to track — and worse, we might [commit them by accident]{.uwred}.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Create a `.gitignore`

Git reads a file named [`.gitignore`]{.uwred} and ignores anything that matches a pattern in it. Create one:

```bash
nano .gitignore
```

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

Add two patterns, then save and exit:

```
*.tmp
receipts/
```

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

[`*.tmp`]{.uwred} matches any file ending in `.tmp`; the trailing slash in [`receipts/`]{.uwred} matches that whole folder and everything inside it.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## The clutter disappears

```bash
git status
```

```
On branch main
Untracked files:
  (use "git add <file>..." to include in what will be committed)
	.gitignore

nothing added to commit but untracked files present (use "git add" to track)
```

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

The scratch files and `receipts/` are gone from the list. The only thing Git still sees is `.gitignore` itself.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Track the `.gitignore` itself

Commit `.gitignore` so the rules travel with the project:

```bash
git add .gitignore
git commit -m "Ignore scratch files and receipts"
```

```
[main d4e5f6a] Ignore scratch files and receipts
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+)
 create mode 100644 .gitignore
```

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

Tracking it means anyone who clones the repo — including [future you]{.uwred} on another computer — ignores the same files automatically.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Ignored means ignored

New files that match keep getting ignored, with no extra work:

```bash
touch results.tmp
git status
```

```
On branch main
nothing to commit, working tree clean
```

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

And if you try to add an ignored file, Git stops you:

```bash
git add scratch.tmp
```

```
The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files:
scratch.tmp
hint: Use -f if you really want to add them.
```

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

That warning is a feature. If you ever truly need to track one, [`git add -f`]{.uwred} forces it.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Common things to ignore

For data science projects, a `.gitignore` usually covers:

<div class="gap-sm"></div>

- [Secrets]{.uwred} — `.env`, API keys, credential files
- [Large or raw data]{.uwred} — `data/`, `*.csv`, `*.parquet`
- [Generated output]{.uwred} — rendered reports, figures, caches
- [Tool cruft]{.uwred} — `.Rhistory`, `.RData`, `.Rproj.user/`, `__pycache__/`

<div class="gap-md"></div>

Many languages and editors publish starter `.gitignore` files you can copy from — GitHub even offers one when you create a repo.

::: {.footer}
Already committed a secret by accident? Ignoring it now won't remove it from past history — see the "Removing Sensitive Data from a Repository" appendix.
:::


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

::: {.callout-important}
# Try it
Bucky keeps a private budget spreadsheet in the folder:

1. Create it with `touch budget.xlsx`
2. Confirm Git sees it with `git status`
3. Add a pattern to `.gitignore` so Git ignores `.xlsx` files
4. Run `git status` again — it should be gone. Then `git add` and `git commit` your updated `.gitignore`
:::
:::


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Where we are

Bucky's repo now ignores the clutter:

- [`.gitignore`]{.uwred} lists patterns for files Git should skip
- Patterns like [`*.tmp`]{.uwred} and [`receipts/`]{.uwred} match files and folders
- We commit `.gitignore` so the rules are shared
